absent: Numeric values and bit positions of dispatch-queue identities, enqueue flags, task flags, runqueue flags, capability bits, operation states and telemetry events.
Full structure definitions for scheduler, runqueue extension, task extension, dispatch queue and per-CPU scheduler state.
Contracts of scheduler callbacks and dispatch helpers such as enqueue, dequeue, dispatch enqueue, direct dispatch, slice programming, bypass selection and error reporting.
Rescue tuning constants including quantum, bandwidth, saturation delta and capacity shift, plus timer and time-base semantics.
Requeue reason encoding, repeat-limit value, sequence-field layout and descendant and online-test helper internals.
Cross-CPU locking and migration ordering beyond the asserted runqueue-held requirements visible here.

findings.text: Main enqueue routine deciding among scheduler callback, direct dispatch, local placement, global placement and bypass placement based on task and runqueue state.
Runqueue online predicate combining scheduler-visible online state with processor activity.
Scheduler clock reader preferring a cached valid runqueue clock and otherwise sampling a fresh per-processor clock.
Detach routine removing a task from its dispatch queue or cancelling deferred local linkage and holding state when no queue is attached.
Unlink helper maintaining queue membership, priority index and cached first task for non-builtin queues.
Local queue resolver enforcing capability requirements and diverting to rescue or reject queues when requirements are unmet.
Online is true only when both the scheduler online flag and processor active state hold, with the latter giving stability of the former across an unlocked scheduling operation.
Enqueue capability need is none under ignore-caps, immediate-enqueue cap for immediate requests, and base enqueue cap otherwise.

Preemption need is none when placement is kernel-forced, when current execution is outside this class, or when current owner is inside the placing subtree; otherwise a dedicated preempt cap is needed, while an alternate build always needs nothing.
Without sub-schedulers the local resolver always selects the runqueue local queue with no capability or diversion logic.

Full resolver checks needed caps against the placing scheduler, force-admits draining, migration-disabled or migration-pending tasks without preemption, and otherwise strips priority and slice request markers before choosing rescue or reject.
Post-enqueue handling leaves scheduler custody with a dequeue notification when applicable, schedules deferred work for reject inserts, and returns early for non-local inserts.

Local post-enqueue handling raises runqueue class visibility for higher-class tasks, skips further wakeup while in dispatch, and otherwise requests current-task slice expiry for preemption requests with denial accounting on failure.
Rescue budget grows with elapsed scheduler time scaled by configured rescue bandwidth, capped lower outside a session and higher inside one, with a saturation shortcut for large gaps.
Rescue immediate admission requires no current rescue holder, an empty rescue wait list, and at least one full quantum of budget; otherwise pacing relies on the rescue timer.
Rescue admission records holder identity, granted slice length and execution snapshot, programs the task slice, and ensures the pacing timer is armed.
Rescue timer arming is idempotent while pending, uses a small fractional quantum as base delay stretched to cover a full-quantum deficit when idle, and expires with round-up on the owning processor.

Remote movement marks the destination before deactivation, reassigns the task processor, hands the runqueue lock to the destination, and stashes enqueue flags plus placing scheduler across activation so capability checks use the placer.
Remote target validation rejects migration-disabled tasks, disallowed processors and offline runqueues, reporting scheduler errors for the first two and only an event for offline.
Deferred local requeue work is drained one record at a time under a dedicated guard with the record cleared and unlinked before the corresponding local scan runs.

Local requeue scan ignores migration-pending tasks and tasks outside the requesting subtree, tags selected tasks with a requeue reason, moves them aside before reinsertion, and clears the tag after each reinsert.
On capability revocation the local scan additionally evicts a currently running capless task of this class by clearing its slice and requesting reschedule.
Unlinking removes priority index membership and list membership, decrements queue count, and refreshes the cached first task for non-builtin queues when the removed task was cached.
Queue count decrement also maintains the runqueue immediate-task count only for the local queue identity and guards against identity mismatch and underflow.
Repeated requeue without running is counted per task, reported after the first repeat, and ejects the owning scheduler past a fixed repeat limit with the task left stranded for scheduler exit.

Fresh enqueues clear persistent immediate marking, while offline, bypassing, exiting, migration-disabled and missing-callback situations avoid the scheduler callback in favor of local, global or bypass targets.
Default slice refill installs the scheduler default without discarding a pending out-of-band request and accounts the refill as an event.
Runqueue lock must be held across rescue accounting and admission, remote movement source handling, deferred draining, local requeue scanning, dequeue and unlink paths, asserted by runtime checks.
Non runqueue-owned queues take their own queue guard during dequeue while runqueue-owned queues rely on the runqueue lock; deferred local records are protected by a dedicated deferred guard.
Clock reader requires either execution on the target processor without preemption or ownership of that runqueue lock.

Runqueue extension observed to carry flags, cached clock, local queue, reject queue, rescue state with holder and budget and timer, immediate count, dispatch state, and stashed remote activation context.

Task extension observed to carry queue linkage, priority node, queue pointer, flags, slice and custody state, sequence and operation state, holding processor, sticky placement, rescue timestamp and capability revocation reasons.
Dispatch queue observed to carry identity, membership count, list and priority index, queue guard, and cached first task pointer for non-builtin queues.
Enqueue operation state moves from none to queueing during the scheduler callback and then either to direct dispatch handling or to queued with custody marking and release ordering for waiters.
Rescue handling cycles among budget accrual, immediate admission when idle and funded, queued waiting with arrival timestamp, and timer-paced retry.

Deferred requeue flows from deferred record insertion to guarded extraction, memory ordering, local scan, task-wise reinsertion, and possible reappearance through the same deferred path bounded by the repeat cap.
Task enqueue routine acts as the scheduling-class entry that classifies internal migration and restore movements separately from fresh scheduler decisions.
Runqueue lock may be released between local enqueue and actual execution, allowing a higher-class wakeup to intervene; class visibility is therefore raised so wakeup preemption can detect it.
Dequeue races with concurrent transfer to a local queue via a holding-processor marker: the loser clears the marker or unlinks membership under the appropriate guard.
Migration-disabled state must be tested before processor affinity because the allowed mask update races with task switch-out and can briefly suggest a movable task.
Queue identities distinguish local, reject, rescue and invalid targets; enqueue request bits distinguish immediate, preempt, head, rescue, requeue, slice control and capability-ignore behaviors.
Telemetry and capability vocabulary includes slice-denied, forced-admit, rescue, requeue-repeat, bypass, skip and offline events, enqueue and preempt caps, and requeue reason and revocation markers.
